title: Reversal of a live machine run
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $c_0$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, let $p$ be a valid input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions, and let $t$ be a natural number. Suppose the configuration reached by $M$ after each time $j<t$ from $c_0$ is not halted. Then the restoration machine, started at the checkpoint for the configuration reached after $t$ steps with the history of those $t$ steps and input-head position $p$, reaches the completed restoration configuration for $c_0$ and $p$ after exactly $2t+1$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols
$c_0$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
$p$ is a valid input-head position among the $|x|+2$ positions
For every $j<t$, the configuration reached from $c_0$ after $j$ steps is not halted
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite machine that is live (not halted) at every time before $t$
when run from $c_0$. Then the restoration machine, started at the checkpoint for
$M$'s time-$t$ configuration with the $t$-step history, reaches the completed
restoration configuration of $c_0$ --- original work tapes and head positions,
blank history --- in exactly $2t + 1$ steps, preserving any supplied input-head
position.
